question: A 29-year-old woman presents with a skin rash that has spread on her arm over the last few days. She also complains of fever, headache, joint pain, and stiffness of the neck associated with the onset of the rash. On physical examination, there is an annular, red rash with a clear area in the center similar to a bull’s-eye (see image). The patient says she went on a camping trip to Connecticut last month but does not remember being bitten by an insect. Which of the following could result if this condition remains untreated in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "29-year-old woman" -> "skin rash on arm" -> "fever, headache, joint pain, neck stiffness" -> "annular, red rash with a bull's-eye appearance" -> "visited Connecticut" -> "possible exposure to Lyme disease" -> "if untreated, can progress to neurological symptoms" -> "Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis" -> 70%

analysis: The patient's presentation with a skin rash spreading on her arm, along with fever, headache, joint pain, and stiffness of the neck, is suggestive of Lyme disease. The characteristic bull's-eye rash (erythema migrans) is a hallmark of Lyme disease. If left untreated, Lyme disease can progress to more serious complications, including neurological issues, cardiac manifestations, and arthritis.
